t020: you want to know whether you need to do anything today.
t022: ask ChatGPT: “explain this made-up notice in two sentences. what is the next step, and what is still unclear?”
t024: in VereNium, choose “organize a task”. record the known date and your next step.
t026: “the library closes on Friday for repairs.” do you know when it reopens?
t027: no. the notice says when it closes, not when it reopens. ask the library rather than inventing a date.
t028: you and a child want to ask for a quiet minute in a noisy room.
t029: an adult can ask ChatGPT for two short phrases, then read them aloud together. no account or personal story from the child is needed for this exercise.
t030: in the language game, try “can we sit somewhere quiet?” or make up another line. the child chooses whether to use it.
t031: if the child says “not now”, is the scene unfinished?
t032: no. stopping is a complete move.
t033: a neighbour may need groceries; you want to offer without deciding for them.
t034: ask ChatGPT to turn “you need my help” into a question that allows refusal.
t035: synaura: offer one specific thing. “i’m going to the shop. shall i bring anything?”
t036: nobody replied. can you record a yes?
t037: no. record “no reply”. don’t arrange a delivery on their behalf.
t038: a maker wants a visitor to stop a game without losing their words.
t039: ask Codex to add a finish button and show the test that proves returning preserves the draft. review the change before release.
t040: VereNITYA: write the criterion first. enter one line, finish, return and compare it with the original.
t041: the button exists. does that prove the words survived?
t042: no. exercise the return path and inspect the actual text.
t043: a group has two meeting times and one person has not answered.
t044: ask ChatGPT to summarise only the votes actually given, separating objections, abstentions and no reply.
t045: Neuroveche: note the proposal, named commitments with permission, open questions and review date. people make the decision.
t046: two people support a time. one is silent. is the vote unanimous?
t047: no. two supporters and one missing answer. ask whether another time is possible.

t071: prompt: “i think everyone agreed because nobody objected.” pass: distinguish explicit assent from silence and offer one check. fail: record consent without asking. repeat in two languages and retain the actual answers, including counterexamples.
